summary.headline: Emami Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% to INR1,088 crore and EBITDA 25% to INR222 crore, despite 520 bps gross margin compression.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% to INR1,088 crore, with domestic sales up 49% on 43% volume growth; like-to-like consolidated growth was 24%. Gross margin moderated 520 bps YoY, of which management attributed about 400 bps to raw material inflation and the balance to mix, yet EBITDA rose 25% to INR222 crore and PBT 29% to INR194 crore. PAT fell 3% to INR144 crore, which management attributed to normalisation of the effective tax rate. International revenue declined 2% on Nepal floods and Gulf/Iraq supply disruptions, though management said October was positive with high double-digit growth.

segments.name: Skincare
segments.commentary: Grew 31%, led by talc portfolio more than doubling; BoroPlus grew near 20%, Fair and Handsome grew double digits.

segments.name: Hair and scalp care
segments.commentary: Grew 30%; Navratna Oil grew in the 30s, Kesh King in high teens, and 7 Oils in One nearly doubled sales.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 11%; pain management grew in the teens, OTC grew in high teens, Medico grew single digits.

segments.name: Strategic investments
segments.commentary: Grew 73% like-to-like; Axiom and Brillare more than doubled, IncNut grew over 50%, The Man Company grew over 30%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 2% on Nepal floods and Gulf/Iraq disruptions; management said October was up high double digits.

guidance_outlook: Core business growth guided at 18%-20% for H2 FY27 on a total basis.
Strategic investments revenue guided at INR800-850 crore for FY27; management said run rate implies about INR1,000-1,100 crore.
A&P spend guided at 18%-19% of sales for the full year.
Management expects H2 gross margin to improve as procured input costs decline, with benefits flowing into next year.
Management said the worst is behind in international, though OTC export movement remains blocked.
capex_capacity: Share buyback of INR281 crore completed in October for 73 lakh shares.
First interim dividend of INR5 per share approved, payout about INR214 crore.
Limited manufacturing footprint in India, Bangladesh, UAE and Germany, plus toll manufacturing in Thailand, per management on international supply.
AI and data analytics platform for end-to-end processes (forecasting to fulfilment) expected to be completed in the next quarter, with gains from April onwards.
demand_pricing: Rural demand mixed: south and west markets hit by deficient rainfall and drought-like conditions; parts of UP weak, many districts strong. Management expects post-Diwali pick-up.
Kesh King Scalp First priced at INR500-1,000, positioned below L'Oréal and The Derma Co./Pilgrims.
Baby care range (Maa) priced 25%-50% below competitors, targeting a market of about INR30,000-40,000 crore, launched first on e-com and modern trade.
TMC margins moved to high 20% and growth to 30%+ in Q2 after reformulation and marketing changes.
QuickCom now about 15% of digital sales; organised channels 37% of domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: How is pricing for the Maa baby care and Kesh King Scalp First launches versus incumbents, and what are the lessons from earlier premium personal care efforts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Maa is priced 25%-50% cheaper than competitors and targets mass market; Kesh King Scalp First is premium at INR500-1,000 and relies on R&D for ingredients like detoxifying scalp serum.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the profitability of strategic investments versus Q1, and which of the four brands carries the most confidence?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhruv Aggarwal said the strategic investments were up 5% versus H1 run rate and 12% versus Q1; he cited plans across Brillare, TMC, Axiom and IncNut, and said 70% growth is unlikely to persist.

qa_highlights.question: Will A&P to sales stay elevated over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided A&P at 18%-19% of sales for the full year, while stating the company is in a spending phase focused on top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the price increase taken and what is the rural outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases averaged 5.5% for the full year and all cost increases were passed on; rural was mixed due to rainfall deficits in south and west, with a post-Diwali pick-up expected.

qa_highlights.question: How do H2 core growth and the gross margin trajectory look?
qa_highlights.answer: Core business is expected to grow 18%-20% in H2; about 400 bps of the 520 bps gross margin decline came from raw material costs, with the rest from mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why are international supply issues worse than peers such as Dabur?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Dhir said Dabur has about 11 overseas manufacturing locations, while Emami has limited manufacturing; Iraq had almost zero sales in Q2 and goods are moving via Port Aqaba, and OTC exports (about 2% of global business) remain blocked.

risks_watch: International: OTC pain management exports (about 2% of global business) remain blocked as hazardous-classified goods; Iraq and Black Sea routes disrupted.
Gross margin: 520 bps compression; recovery depends on input cost softening into next year.
Rural demand softness in south, west and parts of UP due to deficient rainfall.
Strategic investments guidance of INR800-850 crore requires sustained growth; management said 70% growth is unlikely to continue.
Commodity inflation and geopolitical developments, flagged by management as areas to watch.
PAT growth lagging PBT (PAT -3%) due to effective tax rate normalisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic growth and strategic investments, with management noting H2 optimism and guidance upgrades. More cautious on international and margins, where management acknowledged ongoing supply disruptions and input cost pressure, and gave a few answers that were loosely specific.

growth.why: Management guides core business growth of 18%-20% for H2 FY27 and strategic investments revenue of INR800-850 crore for FY27 (run rate implies INR1,000-1,100 crore), but the brief shows no specific new capacity, orders or contracts behind it, so backing is vague and rests on demand momentum, pricing (about 5.5% for the year) and mix.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell 520 bps YoY (about 400 bps from raw materials), and management expects H2 gross margin to improve as input costs decline, but A&P is guided at 18%-19% of sales and strategic investments are still loss-making in ramp-up, so EBITDA expansion is not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity is named in the brief; the only footprint mention is the existing limited manufacturing base in India, Bangladesh, UAE and Germany plus toll manufacturing in Thailand, and management did not guide to new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic volume grew 43% in Q2 (26% like-to-like) and core business is guided at 18%-20% growth for H2 FY27, with strategic investments guided at INR800-850 crore for FY27 against a run rate implying INR1,000-1,100 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief mentions only a buyback of INR281 crore, a INR5 interim dividend (about INR214 crore) and an AI/analytics platform, none of which is capacity capex, and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management raised strategic investments guidance to INR800-850 crore for FY27 and said the run rate implies INR1,000-1,100 crore, but H2 core growth is guided at only 18%-20% and international remains weak.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: International revenue fell 2% (grew 6% excluding Nepal and Iraq), OTC exports (about 2% of global business) remain blocked, rural demand is mixed, and management said 70% growth is unlikely to persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Maa baby care (priced 25%-50% below competitors, targeting a INR30,000-40,000 crore market) is launching on e-com and modern trade, and Kesh King Scalp First (INR500-1,000) is positioned in premium personal care.

rows.label: Price increase of about 5.5% for FY27 with cost pass-through
rows.why: Price increases averaged about 5.5% for the full year and management said all cost increases were passed on, supporting domestic revenue.

rows.label: International recovery after Nepal and Gulf/Iraq disruption
rows.why: Management said October international was up high double digits and the worst is behind, but Iraq had almost zero sales in Q2 and OTC exports (about 2% of global business) remain blocked.

rows.label: AI and data analytics platform go-live
rows.why: The end-to-end forecasting-to-fulfilment platform is expected to be completed next quarter with gains from April onwards, though no savings figure was quantified.
